Running the outer loop in parallel

Source: vignettes/articles/parallel.Rmd
parallel.Rmd

The outer folds of a nested run do not depend on one another, so they can run at the same time. The nested functions send them to mirai daemons (separate R processes) when two or more are connected, and run them one after another otherwise.

library(tidymodels)
library(nestedtune)

The setup

We reuse the design, the random forest and the grid from vignette("nested-cv").

set.seed(1)

folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = vfold_cv(v = 5),
  inside = vfold_cv(v = 5)
)

rf <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger") |>
  set_mode("regression")

wf <- workflow(mpg ~ ., rf)

grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2L, 5L, 8L), min_n = c(2L, 10L))

Running in parallel

We start a pool of two daemons with mirai::daemons(). The call to nested_tune_grid() does not change.

mirai::daemons(2)

set.seed(2)
par_res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = grid)

par_res
#> 
#> ── Nested cross-validation results ────────────────────────────────────
#> Outer resamples: 5-fold cross-validation
#> # A tibble: 5 × 9
#>   splits         id    .metrics .selected .inner_metrics    .notes  
#>   <list>         <chr> <list>   <list>    <list>            <list>  
#> 1 <split [25/7]> Fold1 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 2 <split [25/7]> Fold2 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 3 <split [26/6]> Fold3 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 4 <split [26/6]> Fold4 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> 5 <split [26/6]> Fold5 <tibble> <tibble>  <tibble [12 × 8]> <tibble>
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: .completed <lgl>, .tuning_seed <int>,
#> #   .outer_fit_seed <int>
#> ℹ Use `summary()` for what the run means: which folds failed, what
#>   each one selected, and the estimate across them.

Each fold’s inner tuning runs serially on its daemon, so the two loops do not compete for cores. The first call after starting a pool is slower, because each daemon loads the packages the workflow needs.

mirai::daemons(0) stops the pool, and the same call then runs serially. The parallel section of ?nested_tune_grid says what the daemons load, how to use them under devtools::load_all(), and what an interrupt does.

mirai::daemons(0)

The same result

Each fold takes its seeds by its position in the design, so one seed gives one result serially and in parallel, as ?nested_tune_grid explains.

set.seed(2)
ser_res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = grid)

c(
  metrics = identical(par_res$.metrics, ser_res$.metrics),
  selected = identical(par_res$.selected, ser_res$.selected)
)
#>  metrics selected 
#>     TRUE     TRUE

When a pool pays

On mtcars each fold takes under a second, so two daemons save little time. A pool pays when the folds are expensive: more data, a bigger grid, a slower engine or a costly recipe.
